problem: Internal events are encoded as messages from a process to itself (from P1 to P1, P2 to P2, P3 to P3). In sequence-diagram notation a self-arrow conventionally means a message sent to oneself, so a reader can mistake the internal steps for messages, which contradicts the text saying internal events are not messages. All entries also have dashed set to false, so the internal markers will look the same as real messages.
fix: Draw the internal events as markers or notes on each lifeline (for example an events list with actor and label), not as from-to entries, and keep the two real messages m1 and m2 in the messages list only.

problem: The claim 'A late message cannot arrive after the round ends: its delay is bounded by Δ' only holds if the round is at least Δ long, but round length is never stated. A student can conclude that any round automatically contains every message of that round.
fix: Add that a round must be at least Δ plus the maximum step time long, so a message sent in a round is guaranteed to arrive before that round ends.
